visual_brief.subject: Claude Sonnet 5.5 coding-agent efficiency
verified_context: Anthropic kept Sonnet 5.5 list token pricing unchanged while reporting lower cost per completed task through fewer tokens, tool calls, and execution steps.
For coding-agent workloads, total task economics depend on successful completion, tool use, retries, latency, and human intervention rather than token price alone.
The practical comparison is therefore the amount of work required to reach the same accepted coding result.
visual_brief.editorial_idea: Task efficiency concerns the amount of work needed to reach an accepted result.
visual_brief.visual_metaphor: A winding charcoal route and a shorter terracotta route converge on the same ivory sphere in a tactile paper landscape; the paths are symbolic rather than measured performance data.

candidate_notes.A: Selected. Two sculptural routes meet one centered sphere. The winding charcoal route and shorter terracotta route make the same-result comparison clear at thumbnail size. Paper grain, graphite shading, restrained color, and spatial depth fit both production references. No route length is presented as measured performance.
candidate_notes.B: Constitution-compliant folded physical ribbons meet a blank ivory block. Strong volume, but the shared endpoint sits near the upper-right edge and the heavier folds compete with the outcome.
candidate_notes.C: Constitution-compliant stepped graphite causeway and terracotta arch meet a central sphere. Good silhouette and crop behavior, but stairs introduce an additional effort/elevation metaphor that makes the comparison less direct than A.
